title: Hosted API Region Locking Modes, Retention Profiles & Automated Evidence Synthesis
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and deliver a first-class controls surface for Hosted API tenants to express data residency intent: (1) region locking modes (hard/soft/opt-in), (2) retention profiles with enforcement knobs, and (3) automated evidence synthesis that bundles audit-ready artifacts for compliance reviews. Goal is a minimal, clear UX + corresponding API surfaces and background workers that generate tamper-evident evidence bundles on-demand and on-schedule.
background: Customers increasingly ask for auditable guarantees about where request/response data is stored and how long it is retained. Current hosted controls are limited to coarse region selection and manual exports. Product/security/org have agreed we need stronger primitives: multiple lock modes (for contractual vs. preference cases), first-class retention profiles (per-tenant TTLs + exempt rules), and a reproducible evidence pipeline that teams can consume for audits.
goals: 1) Expose region locking modes in Console & API; 2) Ship retention profile model (default/personal-data-limited/strict) and enforcement pipeline; 3) Implement background evidence exporter that composes logs, storage manifests, KMS-signed manifest, and policy mappings into a zipped evidence bundle; 4) Provide operator audit trail and RBAC for overrides.
non_goals: This ticket does not include private/VPC deployment changes, per-model residency enforcement beyond routing heuristics, or long-term archive lifecycle policies (separate work).
proposed_solution:
- Region locking modes: implement three modes - HARD_LOCK (requests must be routed to specified region(s) only; reject incompatible fallback), SOFT_PREFER (prefer pinned region but allow fallbacks with flags and logged justification), and OPT_IN (tenant chooses to pin sessions manually per-request).
- Retention profiles: tenant-level profile with TTL in days, optional per-route overrides, and allow 'exempted' tags for non-user-generated data (health checks, telemetry). Backend enforcement via retention worker that issues delete jobs and writes deletion manifests.
- Evidence synthesis: scheduled and ad-hoc exporter that assembles: routing traces (per-request region decisions), storage manifests (object keys and regions), retention deletion manifests, policy configuration snapshot, and signed digest. Evidence bundles are time-stamped and signed using KMS-backed signing key. Export formats: tar.gz with JSON manifest and human-readable summary PDF.
- API & Console: new POST /tenants/{id}/residency to set mode; GET /tenants/{id}/residency for status and recent fallback events; UI toggle with explainer and required contract checkbox for HARD_LOCK.
- Operator controls: audit-only preview mode, emergency override endpoint (require SSO MFA + approval), and built-in rate limit for evidence exports to control cost.
api_changes: Add new REST endpoints: POST /tenants/{id}/residency, PATCH /tenants/{id}/retention, GET /tenants/{id}/residency/violations, POST /evidence/tenants/{id}/bundle (ad-hoc). Events emitted to audit-log topic 'residency.events'. SDK bindings to follow in next sprint.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows residency mode and retention profile for tenant; toggles persist and are visible in tenant config
API endpoints return correct mode and retention values; invalid mode transitions rejected (e.g., cannot unset HARD_LOCK without acceptance)
Routing layer respects HARD_LOCK and rejects requests that cannot be fulfilled in pinned region; SOFT_PREFER logs fallbacks to /tenants/{id}/residency/violations
Retention worker deletes objects per TTL and emits deletion manifests that are included in evidence bundles
Evidence bundle contains signed manifest + routing traces + deletion manifests and can be downloaded from Console or via API
RBAC prevents regular operators from performing emergency overrides; overrides require approval flow
Automated nightly evidence export job completes for tenants with residency compliance enabled and retention profile strictness >= 'personal-data-limited'
Security review sign-off completed for KMS usage and bundle signing
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): API + Console read-only surface + evidence exporter for internal tenants. Phase 2 (Beta): Enable set operations for SOFT_PREFER and retention profiles; invite 10 pilot customers. Phase 3 (GA): HARD_LOCK mode with contract checkbox and billing flags; full docs and compliance pack. Feature flag gating per-tenant during rollout.
monitoring_alerts: Alert if nightly evidence job failure rate > 5% over 6 hours
Alert on >1 HARD_LOCK routing rejection per minute per tenant
Audit-log anomalies: unsigned or missing manifests
docs_and_training: Confluence guide: Residency modes and expected guarantees
Runbook for emergency override review and rollback
Customer-facing FAQ and sample compliance pack download flow
Internal training for CSMs and Solutions on how to verify evidence bundles
open_questions: What level of routing determinism is needed to claim 'HARD_LOCK' in SLAs? (engineering input)
Do we allow per-route HARD_LOCK vs tenant-wide? (policy trade-off)
Retention deletions: soft-delete window (7 days) or immediate irrecoverable delete?
Define SLOs for evidence export latency for ad-hoc requests (hours vs minutes)
decisions: Use KMS-backed keys and sign bundle manifests instead of storing proofs in external SCM (accepted 2025-02-25)
Implement SOFT_PREFER as default to reduce customer disruption; HARD_LOCK requires explicit contract acceptance (accepted 2025-02-28)
Evidence bundle format will be tar.gz with JSON manifest + optional PDF summary (accepted 2025-03-02)
